gloss: the camp in favor; supporters; those for

definitions.gloss: the camp in favor; supporters; those for a proposal
definitions.explanation: The group of people who support a particular proposal, plan, or position. Almost always used in contrast with {反対派|はんたいは}, the opposing camp, when describing how opinion on an issue is divided.

examples.japanese: {賛成派|さんせいは}が{多数|たすう}だった。
examples.english: Those in favor were in the majority.

examples.japanese: {議論|ぎろん}は{賛成派|さんせいは}と{反対派|はんたいは}に{分|わ}かれた。
examples.english: The debate split into a camp in favor and a camp against.

examples.japanese: {住民|じゅうみん}への{説明会|せつめいかい}のあと、{賛成派|さんせいは}に{回|まわ}る{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えた。
examples.english: After the briefing for residents, more people came around to supporting it.

notes:
Formed from {賛成|さんせい} (agreement, approval) plus the suffix 〜{派|は} (faction, camp). It names a group of people, not an opinion, so it takes verbs of counting and dividing rather than verbs of thinking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {賛成派|さんせいは}と{反対派|はんたいは}: the camps for and against
- {賛成派|さんせいは}が{多数|たすう}を{占|し}める: supporters make up the majority
- {賛成派|さんせいは}に{回|まわ}る: to come around to supporting
- {賛成派|さんせいは}の{意見|いけん}: the view of those in favor

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {反対派|はんたいは}: the opposing camp — the direct antonym
- {推進派|すいしんは}: the promotion camp — actively pushes a plan forward rather than merely approving of it
